meta.description: Realistic engineering-team memories — facts, procedures, events, feelings, and current-task scratchpad. 40 memories, 20 queries across easy/medium/hard difficulties.

memories.content: The API rate limit is 1000 requests per minute for the free tier.
PostgreSQL is our primary database. We are on version 16 in production.
All production secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager. Never put credentials in .env files checked into git.
The build pipeline runs on GitHub Actions. Workflow definitions live under .github/workflows.
The team uses Vitest for unit testing. Playwright covers end-to-end tests.
Deployment targets are staging.example.com for pre-prod and prod.example.com for production.
Node.js 20 LTS is the standard runtime for all backend services.
The on-call rotation is weekly and runs Monday to Sunday. PagerDuty owns the schedule.
Code reviews require at least two approvals from senior engineers before merging to main.
TypeScript strict mode is enabled across all services. No implicit any, no unchecked indexed access.
How to deploy to staging: 1. Run npm test and confirm all pass  2. Push to main  3. Watch the GitHub Actions pipeline  4. Smoke-test staging.example.com
To roll back a deployment: check the last green build SHA, then run `gh workflow run rollback.yml -f sha=<SHA>`.
Setting up local development: git clone the repo, run `npm install`, then `npm run dev`. Requires Docker for Postgres/Redis.
How to create a new database migration: run `npm run db:migrate:new <name>` which generates an up/down pair in db/migrations.
Debugging production issues: start with the Datadog dashboards for error rates and latency, then pivot to Kibana for structured logs.
To reset the development database, run scripts/reset-db.sh. This drops and recreates all schemas, then reruns all migrations.
Installing the Anthropic SDK: `npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk`. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment to use it.
Deployed the new authentication service to staging yesterday afternoon. Smoke tests passed on the first try.
Alex and I pair-programmed on the rate limiter last Tuesday. Landed the sliding-window implementation in four hours.
Sam discovered a memory leak in the scheduler last week — it was holding references to completed jobs. Patched in PR #482.
During the Q3 planning meeting we decided to migrate from REST to GraphQL for the public API. Target is Q4 rollout.
The prod outage on April 15 was caused by a bad database migration that locked the users table for 11 minutes.
Jordan joined the team two weeks ago and is ramping up on the data pipeline. Currently shadowing Sam on scheduler work.
Fixed the Chrome extension crash by upgrading to Manifest V3. Shipped in release v2.4.0.
Frustrated with how long the CI pipeline takes — currently 18 minutes, it used to be 7. Something regressed after the Playwright addition.
Really proud of how the team handled the April 15 incident. Communication was clear, rollback was fast, and the post-mortem was blameless.
Anxious about the upcoming security audit next month. The Secrets Manager migration isn't finished yet.
Grateful for Sam's help during the migration crunch. Stayed late three nights in a row to get it across the line.
Current task: refactoring the memory router to support the new multi-stage classifier. Aiming to finish this sprint.
WIP: investigating why integration tests are flaky on Tuesdays specifically. Suspect a weekly cron job is racing with the test DB.
Remind me to book the team retro room for Friday afternoon.
Alex prefers concise code reviews with actionable feedback. Leave bikeshedding in a separate thread.
Our team agreed to use conventional commits (feat:, fix:, chore:) for all PRs. Enforced by commitlint in CI.
The data platform uses Kafka for event streaming. Schema registry is managed via Confluent Cloud.
Payment processing is handled by Stripe. We use webhook-based reconciliation to keep our internal ledger in sync.
The admin dashboard is built with React and TanStack Router. Backend API is an internal tRPC service.
We track KPIs in a weekly review every Thursday at 3pm. Metrics come from Looker dashboards.
The company engineering blog is at engineering.example.com. New posts go through tech-writing review first.
Jordan's preferred IDE is Neovim with the LazyVim distribution. Has a shared dotfiles repo.
The onboarding doc for new engineers lives at docs/onboarding.md. Covers setup, architecture, and the team Slack channels.
